name: Winter Orb
oracle_text: As long as this artifact is untapped, players can't untap more than one land during their untap steps.
blocked_sentences: As long as this artifact is untapped, players can't untap more than one land during their untap steps.

needs.what: A player-wide static that caps how MANY matching permanents a player may untap during their untap step -- an effect taking a filter ("land") and a maximum (1), where the untapping player chooses which one permanent untaps and every other match stays tapped. It also needs the untap step to offer that choice as a decision, since today nothing in the untap step ever asks the active player anything.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `skip_untap_step` is the closest static and is the wrong shape: `player_statics.untap_held` marks each permanent matching its `affects` filter and `primitives.untap_all` skips every marked one, so it is an all-or-nothing hold per permanent with no count and no chooser. Writing Winter Orb with it would stop ALL of a player's lands untapping (a strictly harsher card, Rising Waters/Stasis territory), which is exactly the approximation the brief forbids. `untap_during_each_untap_step` is its inverse (untap more, not fewer) and `freeze_opponent_lands` freezes a whole side's lands for mana rather than capping a count. `static_max_per_turn` is unrelated -- the loader only reads it on `free_cast_permission`/flashback grants, not on an untap effect. Nothing in `static_effects` carries a numeric ceiling on an untap step, and `untap_all` has no branch that ever asks a player which permanent to untap.

needs.what: An "as long as this permanent is untapped" gate on a static ability -- the static switches off while its own source is tapped, which is how Winter Orb is answered (tap the Orb on the opponent's end step).
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `static_condition_keys` offers `counters`, `cmp`, `exists`, `is_attached`, `is_your_turn`, `top_of_library` and the boolean combinators. `exists` over `{"self_only": true, "tapped": false}` is the near miss and may well read the source's tapped state, but it is unproven for a self-referential untapped check and is worthless without the capping effect above, so it is recorded here rather than guessed at.
